_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from the project's own documentation; no upstream egg.
name: CoreDNS
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: CoreDNS is a small, flexible DNS server configured with a Corefile. The egg starts it as a caching resolver that answers only the clients you allow and forwards their queries upstream; most devices only use DNS on port 53, so give the server that port if the node allows it.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# CoreDNS: downloads CoreDNS from its GitHub releases, checked against
# GitHub's SHA-256, and writes a starting Corefile if there's none. An
# existing Corefile and zone files are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) echo "CoreDNS has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))."; exit 1 ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag coredns/coredns "$version") || exit 1

if [ -x coredns ] && [ "$(cat .coredns-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "CoreDNS $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading CoreDNS $tag."
    gh-release download coredns/coredns "$tag" "coredns_${tag#v}_linux_${arch}.tgz" "$work/coredns.tgz"
    tar -xzf "$work/coredns.tgz" -C "$work"
    install -m 0755 "$work/coredns" coredns.new
    mv -f coredns.new coredns
    echo "$tag" > .coredns-version
fi

if [ ! -f Corefile ]; then
    cat > Corefile <<'COREFILE'
# CoreDNS's configuration: https://coredns.io/manual/toc/
# It listens on the server's port. raptor-settings.conf is written at every
# start from the Upstream resolvers and Allowed clients settings in Startup:
# only the clients you allow are answered (an open resolver gets abused), and
# their queries are forwarded upstream. Changes to this file are picked up
# within a minute, without a restart.
. {
    import raptor-settings.conf
    cache 300
    errors
    reload
    loop
}
COREFILE
    echo "Wrote a starting Corefile that forwards queries to the upstream resolvers."
fi
echo "Installed CoreDNS $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The CoreDNS release to install, such as 1.15.0, or latest.

variables.name: Upstream resolvers
variables.description: Where queries are forwarded, separated by spaces: addresses such as 1.1.1.1, or tls://1.1.1.1 for DNS over TLS.

variables.name: Allowed clients
variables.description: The addresses CoreDNS answers, as CIDR ranges separated by spaces; add your own public address as 203.0.113.7/32. Everyone else is refused.
